analysis.evidence: אֵת כָּל־הָרְכֻשׁ marks all the possessions as the direct object. The verse repeats the verb as הֵשִׁיב when it says that Abram also brought back Lot and his possessions.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces a Hiphil wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with Abram as the subject.

analysis.evidence: אֵת introduces כָּל הָרְכֻשׁ, “all the possessions,” as the definite direct object of וַיָּשֶׁב, “he brought back.”
analysis.morphology: Hebrew direct-object marker with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיָּשֶׁב אֵת כָּל הָרְכֻשׁ, “he brought back all the property,” כָּל refers to the full amount of property recovered.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state, with הָרְכֻשׁ as its complement.
